chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sufyan ibn al-Simṭ, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Clipping the nails, trimming the moustache, and washing the head with the hibiscus plant removes poverty and increases sustenance.
ai.seo_question: What are the benefits of clipping nails and trimming the moustache in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Al-Kafi connects physical tidiness (fitrah) with divine blessing, specifically highlighting the use of hibiscus (khitammi) for its cooling and purifying properties. Scholars interpret the removal of poverty not merely as material wealth but as the alleviation of spiritual and worldly burdens through adherence to prophetic grooming practices. This act serves as a tangible manifestation of inner purity, reinforcing the link between bodily care and spiritual elevation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Sufyan Bin Al Samt, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Clipping the nails, and taking from the moustache, and washing the head with the hibiscus negates the poverty and increases in the livelihood’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Sufyan af-Simt who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Cutting fingernails, trimming the mustache and washing the head with marshmallow plant banish poverty and increases one’s sustenance.’”
